decisions.finding: seg4 'three smooth waves for the time of year' is unexplained; the learner would not recognise it in an assistant's output or know why three
decisions.reason: SPEC voice rule: explain a term the first time or do not use it. 'Three waves' is how the model is built (forecast.regression_model.what: 'three yearly waves'), but the count is nothing the learner sees in an output or needs to direct the work. 'A smooth curve for the time of year' is still true, matches the brief's 'time-of-year terms', and sets up seg6 (a smooth curve cannot single out one week in late November).
decisions.change: seg4 narration: 'three smooth waves for the time of year' -> 'a smooth curve for the time of year'. Nothing else in the segment changed.

rulings.R1: seg2, one sentence added at the end: 'The idea is general: any daily count, say next month's support tickets for staffing, is forecast from its trend, its rhythm and its known dates.'
rulings.R3: ask_assistant rewritten as a paste-ready template (116 words) with slots [series], [day or week], [horizon], [weekday], [week], [four], [event dates], [twelve], [month starts], [month]. Every demand for evidence kept: all methods scored on the same forecasts, each trained only on data before its forecast date, average and worst period per method, the event dates listed back, each forecast's last training date, fitted effects in percent.
rulings.R4: seg9 cut from 85 to 42 words, two sentences (what the learner now does when finance asks for a number; pointer to 6-2). It no longer re-reads the take-aways. Quote visual kept.

Four 'nothing is wrong' distractors replaced by specific mistakes of similar length: quiz q2 B ('Nothing more ...' -> asking for a steadier average over more monthly forecasts), quiz q3 A ('Nothing ...' -> a longer 90-day window), review 1 v2 C ('None ...' -> a second, more complex model's error), review 1 v3 D ('None ...' -> the team's own target). The 'why' of quiz q2 and q3 gained a clause each so it still covers the tempting wrong option. All keyed answers unchanged.
rulings.R6: seg8, one sentence replacing 'No code reading required.': 'And for a small decision a few weeks out, a four week average in a spreadsheet, adjusted by hand for known events, will do.' (the run-rate alternative that sat only in other_ways).

open_questions: Narration is exactly 900 words, the SPEC ceiling: R1 and R6 each add a sentence and the shorter recap pays for them. Any further spoken addition to this lesson needs a cut elsewhere.
